name: capell-app/widget-countdown
description: A countdown for any page, ticking down days, hours, minutes and seconds to your event and showing your own message at zero.

marketplace.summary: Show visitors how long is left until a wedding, open day, launch or deadline, with the date written out in full above the digits.
marketplace.description: Place a countdown on a page in Layout Builder and visitors see the days, hours, minutes and seconds ticking down below the date written out in full. Give it a title, a target time, the message to show at the end and an optional button with a link. At zero the digits stay on the page and your message appears beneath them. You type the event's local time in the time zone you choose, which starts as UTC, and summer time is applied for you. Screen readers announce the time left when it loads and let visitors know when it ends.
marketplace.problem: Guests and visitors keep asking how long is left until our event.
marketplace.outcome: The time left ticks down on the page, with the date written out in full and your message appearing at zero.

faq.question: How do I set the time for an event in another time zone?
faq.answer: Choose the time zone the event happens in, for example Europe/London, then enter the start time as it reads there. Clock changes are handled for you. The time zone box starts as UTC, so change it first.

faq.question: What do visitors see when it reaches zero?
faq.answer: The numbers stop at zero and the end message you wrote appears under them.

faq.question: Does it work if the visitor's browser blocks scripts?
faq.answer: Partly. The live ticking and the end message need a small script in the browser. Without it, visitors see the date written out and how much time remained when the page was built.

faq.question: Can I add a button to a countdown?
faq.answer: Yes. A countdown can have one optional button with a link.

faq.question: What do I need to put a countdown on a page?
faq.answer: Layout Builder, the page builder. Add the Countdown block there and fill in its title, target time and end message.
